newsitem.title: UK: Next up amid positive press, analyst comment.
newsitem.headline: Next up amid positive press, analyst comment.

text.p: Shares in Next Plc rose on Monday after positive weekend press comment and after analysts at Morgan Stanley repeated their positive outlook for the retailer while renewing coverage of the stock with a "neutral' rating.
By 1138 GMT the shares were up 17p at 574-1/2p in relatively thin volume.
"I resumed coverage of the stock with a neutral rating," Victoria Melendez, stores analyst at Morgan Stanley, said.
"Although I am positive on the company I think that at current price levels the shares are fairly valued by most valuation criteria."
Melendez added that despite the stock rating, she was impressed with the company's performance and would seek buying opportunities at lower levels.
"I am looking for around 17 percent compound annual growth in profits over the next three years," said the analyst, adding that for the current year pretax profit was seen rising 24.5 percent.
In a report in the Observer on Sunday, analysts at Mees Pierson attributed Next's success to its premium brand image.

The newspaper also cited Next's chief executive David Jones saying future plans for stores included an increase in floor space, a wider range of accessories, petite and tall clothes, shoes and babywear.
Over the past year shares in the company have outpaced the FTSE All-Share index by 22.5 percent, but over the past five years they out performed the index by 813 percent.
"The shares are unlikely to continue this strong outperformance in the forthcoming months," Melendez said.
